init.welcome:
sdlc — Software Development Lifecycle harness

This wizard sets up OpenSpec and the SDLC harness for the coding tools you choose.
Nothing is written until you confirm the summary at the end.
init.mode.block: block — hooks deny actions that skip a gate
init.statusline: Install the Claude Code status line?
init.mcp: Register sdlc as an MCP server for the chosen tools, so other AI systems can read the process?
init.indexCodegraph: Index this project with codegraph and connect it to the chosen tools only?

init.layoutChoice.adapt: adapt - keep the documents where they are, record them, create the missing ones
init.layoutChoice.none: none - leave the documents as they are

workflow.help.title: SDLC: Help
workflow.help.description: Show available SDLC workflows and the current project state.
workflow.next.title: SDLC: Next
workflow.next.description: Advance an SDLC change to its next step in the AI-native lifecycle (intent, spec, plan, build, verify, review, release, archive). Use when the user says "continue", "next step", "what's next", or wants to move a change forward without naming the stage.
workflow.status.title: SDLC: Status
workflow.status.description: Show the SDLC dashboard - every active change with its stage (plan, design, build, test, deploy), gate states, approvals, verification and review status, and who must act next. Use when the user asks for status, progress, what is blocked, or what needs approval.
workflow.adopt.title: SDLC: Adopt
workflow.adopt.description: Prepare an existing project for agents: check the layout, fill the documents from the code, draft the settings and roles for a person to apply.
workflow.backlog.title: SDLC: Backlog
workflow.backlog.description: See the backlog, decompose an epic or idea into items, bring an item to ready and start it, through the backlog commands.
workflow.explore.title: SDLC: Explore
workflow.explore.description: Research and pressure-test an idea before deciding whether to write intent.
workflow.intent.title: SDLC: Intent
workflow.intent.description: Capture an idea, request, ticket or problem as intent.md, the Stage 1 (Plan) artifact of the AI-native SDLC, for product-owner approval. Use when the user describes something they want built or fixed, or says "new idea", "capture intent", "start a change".
workflow.spec.title: SDLC: Spec
workflow.spec.description: Turn an accepted intent into the requirements and design spec (Stage 2, Design) - OpenSpec proposal.md, delta specs and design.md with policies applied and areas of concern flagged. Use after the intent gate is approved, or when the user asks to write or refine requirements or the design.
workflow.plan.title: SDLC: Plan
workflow.plan.description: Produce the implementation plan (Stage 3, Build) from an approved spec - plan.md (files that change, order of work, risks, proof, rollback) and tasks.md - for engineer approval before any code is written. Use after the spec gate is approved or when the user asks for an implementation plan.
workflow.build.title: SDLC: Build
workflow.build.description: Implement an SDLC change from its approved plan (Stage 3, Build) with a continuous feedback loop - work through tasks.md, run the project's checks after each step, keep plan.md in sync. Use when the plan gate is approved and the user asks to implement, build, or apply the change.
workflow.verify.title: SDLC: Verify
workflow.verify.description: Verify an implemented SDLC change (Stage 4, Test) - run the project's checks with `sdlc verify` to record literal evidence, then get an independent behavioral verification against the spec scenarios in a fresh context. Use after implementation, or when the user asks to test, verify, or check that a change works.
workflow.review.title: SDLC: Review
workflow.review.description: Review a verified SDLC change (Stage 5, Deploy) in independent passes - bugs, security, compliance with the spec, plan and design principles in REVIEW.md - record severity-ranked findings in review.md, fix the important ones, and hand off to a human code owner. Use when the user asks for a review, a PR review, or to address review findings.
workflow.release.title: SDLC: Release
workflow.release.description: Prepare an approved SDLC change for release (Stage 5, Deploy) - release.md with changelog, per-environment rollout, monitoring signals and a rehearsed rollback - up to the production gate, which a release manager authorizes. Use when the user asks to release, ship, or deploy a change.
workflow.archive.title: SDLC: Archive
workflow.archive.description: Close a completed SDLC change - confirm every required gate is satisfied, merge its delta specs into the living specs via OpenSpec archive, and capture learnings (evals, CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md rules, follow-up intents). Use when the user asks to archive, finish, or close a change.
workflow.triage.title: SDLC: Triage
workflow.triage.description: Close the loop (Stage 6, Maintain) - turn an alert, incident, failing build, security finding or ticket into a diagnosed, evidence-backed intent.md that re-enters the lifecycle. Use when the user pastes an alert, incident, error report or scan finding, or asks to investigate a production problem.
hook.separationOfDuties: Gate approvals, rejections, waivers, test unlocks, track selection and backlog priority are human decisions. Ask the responsible person to run `{command}` in their own terminal, not in the agent chat (a `!` command there runs in the agent's shell and is refused too).
hook.stateIntegrityBash: .sdlc.yaml and openspec/.sdlc/log.jsonl hold gate approvals, evidence and the audit log; only the sdlc CLI may change them. Use `sdlc` commands instead of editing them.
hook.stateIntegrityEdit: .sdlc.yaml and openspec/.sdlc/log.jsonl hold gate approvals, evidence and the audit log; only the sdlc CLI may change them.
hook.backlogIntegrity: openspec/backlog.md is changed through the CLI: refine items with `sdlc backlog add` or `sdlc backlog edit`; the order and removal of items are a person's decision (`sdlc backlog move`, `sdlc backlog drop`).
hook.guardConfig: {path} configures the sdlc guard (enforcement mode, hooks, plugin, MCP servers); an agent may not change it. Ask a person to make the change themselves; `sdlc update` restores the generated files.
hook.agentMarker: `CLAUDECODE`, `OPENCODE`, `AGENT` and `SDLC_AGENT` tell the sdlc CLI that an agent is running it; unsetting or blanking them would let an agent pass for a person, so this command is refused. Run it without touching these variables; human decisions are made by a person in their own terminal.
hook.releaseGate: This looks like a production release (matched /{pattern}/). Production releases need a named release authorization: a release manager runs `sdlc approve release --change <id>` after reviewing release.md (or sets SDLC_RELEASE_APPROVAL for this session). The agent prepares the release; it does not authorize it.
hook.protectedPath: {path} is a protected path (enforcement.protected_paths in openspec/sdlc.yaml). Change it through its owning process, not in an agent session.
hook.secretInEdit: Secret in {file}: {kinds}. Do not write keys, tokens or passwords into the project; use an environment variable or a secret store reference instead. A person can exempt test data in enforcement.secret_allow (openspec/sdlc.yaml).
hook.secretKindAssignment: password or token assigned in the code
hook.testsLocked: Tests are locked for change '{change}' (fix-first protocol): the failing test is the proof, so fix the code, not {path}. A person can unlock with `sdlc tests unlock --change {change}`.
hook.planGateNone: No SDLC change covers this edit ({path}). Nothing is implemented without an accepted plan: start with /sdlc:intent (or `sdlc new <name>`), or keep the edit out of scope.
hook.planGatePending: No active change has an approved plan yet ({changes}). Finish the plan and have an engineer run `sdlc approve plan --change <id>` before editing {path}.
hook.verifyBeforeStop: Change '{change}' has all tasks checked but no passing verification for the current code ({detail}). Run `sdlc verify --change {change}` and paste the evidence before finishing.
session.header: SDLC harness ({stamp}): active changes in openspec/changes (run `sdlc status` for details).
session.enforcement: Enforcement mode is {mode}. Gate approvals are made by people with `sdlc approve`, never by the agent.
gate.stale: content changed after approval; re-approval needed
gate.noArtifacts: schema '{schema}' has no artifacts for this gate
gate.verifyStale: code changed since the last passing `sdlc verify`
gate.verifyNoCommands: no verification commands configured (verify.commands in openspec/sdlc.yaml)
gate.noReview: no review.md yet (run the review workflow)
report.title: {name} SDLC progress ({since} to {until})
report.summaryLine: {active} active · {archived} archived · {blocked} blocked · {awaiting} awaiting a person
report.leadLine: Intent to spec: {a} · Spec to plan: {b} · Plan to verified: {c} · Verified to review: {d} · Created to archived: {e}
report.html.title: {name} · SDLC progress

adopt.heading: Adoption draft
adopt.roles: Roles (written to {path} only if it does not exist):

option.clearGoal: remove the goal of the epic
option.initTools: claude,opencode | all | none (default: detected, else both)
option.initCli: how agents invoke the CLI, e.g. "npx --no-install sdlc" for a project-local install
option.noHooks: do not install Claude Code hooks
option.opsx: also install OpenSpec's own /opsx workflows for the same tools
option.statusline: install the Claude Code status line
option.mcp: register sdlc as an MCP server for the chosen tools (mcp.serve in openspec/sdlc.yaml)
option.language: artifact language for a new OpenSpec config
option.forceOverwrite: overwrite generated files even if edited locally
option.initLayout: AI-ready documents: scaffold | adapt | worktree | none (default: none)
option.initWorktree: folder for the new AI-ready worktree (with --layout worktree)
option.gitInit: run git init when the folder is not a git repository
option.updateTools: change the configured tools (claude,opencode | all | none)
option.uninstallForce: also remove generated files that were edited locally
option.newKind: feature | bugfix | refactor | chore | docs | incident | security
option.newRisk: low | medium | high (high adds tech-lead approvals)
option.newTrack: full (all gates) | lite (starts at plan; intent and spec optional)
option.newSourceType: idea | ticket | incident | alert | scan | review | exploration | other
option.sourceRef: external record id (Jira, incident, finding) for linkage
option.skipSpecs: no externally visible behavior changes (sets skip_specs in .openspec.yaml)
option.markdown: markdown report (for pull requests and wikis)
option.nextChange: change id (defaults to the only active change)
option.approveAs: role you approve as (e.g. product-owner, tech-lead, engineer, code-owner)
option.decisionNote: reason or comment (required for reject and waive)
option.decider: override the git identity recorded as the decider
option.only: run only these checks (comma-separated; never passes the gate)
option.checkScenarios: report spec scenarios missing from the behavioral verification table
option.strict: with --check: exit non-zero when scenarios are uncovered
option.reviewBase: base ref for the diff (default: review.base or origin/HEAD)
option.archiveForce: archive past unsatisfied gates (human only, needs --note)
option.licensee: licensee named in the commercial agreement
option.pluginCli: how the plugin invokes the CLI (default: sdlc)
option.marketplace: also write ../.claude-plugin/marketplace.json next to the plugin dir
cmd.takeover: Take a change over from the agent: no agent edits of its files until you hand it back (human only)
cmd.release-control: Hand a taken-over change back to the agent with a note (human only)
option.takeoverNote: why you take the change over (required; the agent sees it)
error.change_x_is_already_taken_over: {change} is already taken over by {by}; hand it back first with `sdlc release-control`.
error.change_x_is_not_taken_over: {change} is not taken over by anyone; there is nothing to hand back.
takeover.taken: {change} taken over by {by}: {note}. The agent may not edit it until you run `sdlc release-control --change {change} --note ...`.
takeover.released: {change} handed back to the agent by {by}: {note}
next.takenOver: Taken over by {by}: {note}. The agent waits until the person hands it back with `sdlc release-control`.
hook.takeover: {change} is taken over by {by} ({note}); the agent may not edit {path} until the person hands it back with `sdlc release-control --change {change}`.
hook.takeoverPaused: {change} is taken over by {by} ({note}) and has no plan.md, so the agent is paused in the whole project until the person hands it back with `sdlc release-control --change {change}`.
hook.takeoverCli: {change} is taken over by {by} ({note}); the agent may not run `{command}` on it until the person hands it back with `sdlc release-control --change {change}`. Read-only steps (`status`, `next`, `trace`, `audit`) still work.
hook.cliRemoval: The sdlc CLI keeps the lifecycle records and checks that human decisions are made by a person; an agent may not uninstall it. Ask a person to remove it in their own terminal if that is really wanted.
cmd.rework: Send a change back to a gate's stage with a reason - human only
option.reworkReason: why the change goes back: a category from rework.reasons in sdlc.yaml
option.reworkAs: role you send the change back as
option.reworkReset: restore the planned files and the change folder from the gate checkpoint
error.rework_needs_note: A rework needs --note "<what has to change>" so the author knows what to redo.
error.rework_gate_not_reached: The change has not reached the {gate} gate yet: nothing was approved at it or after it.
error.rework_no_plan: --reset needs plan.md in the change {change}: its "Files that change" section lists the files to restore.
error.rework_no_checkpoint: There is no checkpoint for the {gate} gate ({ref}): it was approved before checkpoints existed or outside a git repository.
error.rework_dirty_files: These files have uncommitted edits; commit or discard them first. Nothing was restored: {files}
error.rework_reset_through_link: --reset will not write through a symbolic link or junction (the file would land outside the project): {files}. Replace the link with the real file, commit, and run it again.
error.by_not_allowed: Without openspec/roles.yaml, --by is unverified text, so it cannot add an approver to a gate that needs {min} different people. Each person approves without --by under their own git identity, or set up roles.yaml (`sdlc roles migrate`).
rework.nothingRestored: Nothing to restore: the files already match the {gate} checkpoint.
rework.externalNotUndone: External actions (publishing, notifications) are not undone.
context.staleNote: Stale: updated {updated}, older than {days} days. Check it with {owner} before relying on it.

session.guide: The user can ask how sdlc works (stages, approvals, roles, why the hook said no): answer from `sdlc guide`.
